input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: § 8.2 meets the preferred position in full: renewals are for successive twelve-month (not multi-year) terms, Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand — with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which is better than preferred for us. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, matching the preferred cap. § 8.1 sets a three-year master term but expressly does not create multi-year auto-renewal of Order Forms. No redline needed.
